Note: the head said zones_extra Ossuary files; the Ossuary zone actually lives at roblox/src/server/OssuaryZone.luau (zones_extra holds 11 other zones). mountain_check GATE PASS (exit 0): Luau type warnings fired in files this lane did not touch, but the gate rebuilt the_mountain.rbxlx and exited 0 on first run; no rerun needed. Estate grep: corpus/steal/ has ZERO hits for both 'ossuary' and 'seasonal' (first-class negative: the 8-agent intel wave filed to watch/inbox per memory/corpus/LINKS.jsonl but never left a steal receipt in corpus/steal/); memory/corpus/LINKS.jsonl holds the wave-complete and game-mapping records for both terms. All 5 quotes byte-verified grep -F count >= 1; raw counts in a02-ossuary.quotes.txt (SEASONAL_LAUNCH.md quotes are hard-wrapped at 80 chars with 2-space continuation indent, so verification joined newlines and squeezed spaces before grep -F).

rows.law: Pre-register the kill condition: a numeric session floor gates launch, and tuning happens before launch, not after.
rows.claim: SEASONAL_LAUNCH.md fixes a measurable launch gate before playtest: the Ossuary must hold a 3-minute median session or the maze density/darkness is wrong and must be tuned pre-launch.
rows.quote: If the Ossuary cannot hold a 3-minute median session in playtest, the maze density or darkness is wrong; tune before launch, not after.
rows.steal: Write the numeric kill condition into the launch doc BEFORE the playtest that can trigger it; Mag zone and workflow launches get the same pre-registered falsifier, not a postmortem metric.
rows.falsifier: If playtests ship with no measured median session length, or launch proceeds despite a sub-3-minute median, the law is dead letter and the row collapses.

rows.law: When a state flip reads as lag, the fix is a louder signal, never a reinterpretation of the mechanic.
rows.claim: The doc pre-registers stare-feedback ambiguity as a signal deficit, and the code already pairs the freeze bit with a bone-white vs hunting-red color flip set in the same tick as the observed raycast (OssuaryZone.luau line 444).
rows.quote: If the freeze mechanic reads as broken (players think sentinels lag), the stare-feedback is too subtle: ship the eye-glow state flip louder.
rows.steal: Bind a visible channel (color, label, log line) to every binary agent state (frozen/hunting, dormant/dispatch) in the same tick as the state bit; treat user-reported lag as a signal-deficit hypothesis first.
rows.falsifier: If a sentinel changes color without the observed raycast flipping, or the flip never reaches the client, the feedback pair is broken and the law is falsified.

rows.law: A reward faucet without a sink inflates the whole economy; cap at the faucet and register the cap before the faucet opens.
rows.claim: NEGATIVE FINDING: the doc pre-registers the candy cap falsifier, but OssuaryZone.luau pays 2 VM per CandyBone (x2 with CandyDoublerUntil, line 244) and drops 40 candy on felling the Skeleton King with no per-floor daily cap implemented anywhere in the zone.
rows.quote: If Candy Bones inflow exceeds Exchange sink, the economy prints VM and the Steal-a wheel deflates: cap candy per floor per day if needed.
rows.steal: Land the per-floor daily candy cap before the Oct 9 full launch; a falsifier that exists only in the doc while the code ships the uncapped faucet is debt, exactly like a registered-but-unenforced ratchet.
rows.falsifier: If one king felling plus normal pickups can exceed any floor's daily VM budget (40 candy x 2 VM = 80 VM instantly, king Felled resets after 30s, line 347), the uncapped faucet is live and the economy law is already violated.

rows.law: An enemy that moves only when unobserved makes attention the resource, and the shield needs an exception or camping wins.
rows.claim: Weeping-angel sentinels freeze on raycast-verified observation within 40 studs on the same floor, flip bone-white/hunting-red, glide at the player while unobserved, and still kill on touch while observed: the stare shields only at distance (OssuaryZone.luau line 454).
rows.quote: the stare shields at distance; touch does not
rows.steal: Pressure design for harness agents: a watcher freezes a worker, but proximity contact still escalates; observation is a partial shield (review gates slow, never stop), and the exception is what keeps the arbitration honest.
rows.falsifier: If a player can freeze a sentinel and stand inside its touch radius indefinitely, or the observation raycast passes through maze walls, the look-away arbitration is broken.

rows.law: Seasonal spikes convert to evergreen only with a core loop plus post-window updates; the anti-cliff update is part of the launch, not a followup.
rows.claim: The plan books an Aftermath update by Nov 6 that converts trimmed event content to permanent and publishes the November roadmap, explicitly to blunt the community-ruled 15-30% post-event retention cost; the doc's own DOORS evidence base is the proof condition.
rows.quote: convert to evergreen ONLY with a core loop + post-November updates
rows.steal: Every Mag seasonal push (Hermes dispatch windows, gala batteries) gets a scheduled aftermath step that files durable artifacts to the shared surface before the window closes; the cliff is planned against, not hoped away.
rows.falsifier: If the Aftermath update slips past Nov 6 or ships without the November roadmap, the anti-cliff move is falsified and the 15-30% retention cost lands as written.
